claims.text: ECG for everyone: arrhythmia, conduction abnormality, ventricular hypertrophy, pre-excitation, QT prolongation, Brugada, pacemaker malfunction, ischemia or MI.
claims.quote: ECG is done for all patients. The ECG may reveal arrhythmia, a conduction abnormality, ventricular hypertrophy, pre-excitation, QT prolongation, Brugada syndrome, pacemaker malfunction, myocardial ischemia, or myocardial infarction

claims.text: Diagnosis still in doubt: cardiac biomarkers and serial ECGs to rule out MI in older patients, plus ECG monitoring for at least 24 hours.
claims.quote: If the diagnosis is questionable after this basic evaluation, measuring cardiac biomarkers and obtaining serial ECGs to rule out MI in older patients plus ECG monitoring for at least 24 hours are prudent.

claims.text: Pulse oximetry during or right after an episode; hypoxemia calls for CT angiography to rule out pulmonary embolism.
claims.quote: Pulse oximetry should be done during or immediately after an episode to identify hypoxemia (which may indicate pulmonary embolism). If hypoxemia is present, CT angiography is indicated to rule out pulmonary embolism.

claims.text: Labs only by suspicion: pregnancy test in all females of childbearing age; hematocrit if anemia is suspected; electrolytes if an abnormality is suspected; troponin if MI is suspected.
claims.quote: Laboratory tests are done based on clinical suspicion; reflexively obtained laboratory panels are of little use. However, all females of childbearing age should have a pregnancy test. Hematocrit is measured if anemia is suspected. Electrolytes are measured only if an abnormality is clinically suspected (eg, by symptoms or medication use). Serum troponin is measured if acute myocardial infarction is suspected.

claims.text: Echocardiography for unexplained or exercise-induced syncope, murmurs, or suspected intracardiac tumor.
claims.quote: Echocardiography (either point-of-care ultrasound [POCUS] or a traditional echocardiogram) is indicated for patients with clinically unexplained syncope, exercise-induced syncope, cardiac murmurs, or suspected intracardiac tumors (eg, those with positional syncope).

claims.text: Stress testing when intermittent ischemia is suspected; tilt table testing when the history suggests reflex (vasodepressor) syncope.
claims.quote: Stress testing (exercise or pharmacologic) is done when intermittent myocardial ischemia is suspected. It is often done for patients with exercise-induced symptoms. Exercise testing is less valuable unless physical activity precipitated syncope. Tilt table testing may be done if history and physical examination indicate vasodepressor or other reflex-induced syncope.

claims.text: EEG only if a seizure disorder is suspected; head CT or MRI only with signs of a focal CNS disorder.
claims.quote: EEG is warranted if a seizure disorder is suspected. CT and MRI of the head and brain are indicated only if signs and symptoms suggest a focal CNS disorder.
